All three commits are pushed and **both platforms build clean** (macOS + iOS). Here's the complete picture of what shipped this session.

## What was wrong, and what I changed

### A — Photo OCR gibberish / "stuck on English, can't read Mandarin" ✅
Root cause (verified by reading the code + a 9-agent comprehension pass): `PhotoTextRecognitionService` hardcoded `recognitionLanguages = ["en-US","en-GB",…]` **English-first** with `usesLanguageCorrection = true`, and language detection ran *after* OCR on already-garbled text. Vision applied an English model to Chinese glyphs → Latin gibberish, and nothing could switch it.
- Recognition language is now driven by a **`PhotoScanLanguage`** preference (Auto / 中文 / English / Both) — Chinese is listed first and correction is disabled for Chinese.
- New **CJK-ratio-first detector** (`detectLanguageRobust`) replaces the English-biased `NLLanguageRecognizer` routing; the OCR result now carries its detected language; EXIF orientation is honored; Chinese text is cleaned without English regex.
- The photo screen got a **scan-language menu + "重新识别"** button so you can force a language on the same image; the live camera now passes `.text(languages:)`.
- Verified with a standalone logic test: **9/9** (pure/traditional/mixed Chinese all route correctly; whitespace cleaning preserves embedded Latin).

### B — Cloud AI providers with API-fetched models ✅
- `AIProvider` now has **10 providers**: OpenAI, Claude, DeepSeek, Doubao, Qwen, Kimi, Zhipu, MiniMax (+ Apple Intelligence, Ollama), each with REST metadata.
- New **`CloudAIService`** (URLSession, no new dependencies): OpenAI-compatible + Anthropic chat, **vision**, and **model listing via the provider's `/models` API** with curated-default fallback.
- API keys stored in the **Keychain** (`KeychainHelper`); per-provider key/model/base-URL config via a shared **`AIProviderConfigView`** wired into both macOS and iOS settings.
- **Critical latent fix:** the sandboxed app was missing `com.apple.security.network.client` — added it (this also unblocks Ollama on macOS).

### C — Photo → AI cleanup toggle ✅
A settings toggle (`aiPhotoCleanupEnabled`) routes OCR text — and the image itself for vision-capable providers — through the selected model to fix recognition errors before analysis.

### D — Bilingual ✅
- **Learner-mode** setting (English-centric / Mandarin-centric / Bilingual) that adapts the default translation direction app-wide.
- **Dual-language narration** in the word-detail views (Mandarin + English speak buttons).

### "Properly linked up through structured output" (your latest ask) ✅
- **TranslateView's AI buttons now fire for *any* configured provider**, not just Apple Intelligence — so cloud/Ollama responses are actually used (this was the main missing link).
- `response_format: json_object` is sent only where supported (OpenAI/DeepSeek/Kimi/Qwen); others get JSON via prompt + **tolerant `{…}` extraction** (handles fenced/prose-wrapped output — verified 5/5).
- New **structured feature**: "AI 提取重点词汇" on the photo screen asks the model for typed `ExtractedVocabItem[]` (term / reading / meaning) and saves them to the vocab book.
- Decoders are now **tolerant of missing fields**, so a partial model response still renders.

## Verification

- Logic tests: detection/cleaning **9/9**, structured JSON parsing **5/5**.
- Commits pushed to `origin/april-14-2026-ollama`: `4981a25`, `aa020f8`, `4770c8c`.

## The 401 — not an app bug

I reproduced your exact failure outside the app by making the **same** `GET /models` request the app makes:

| Endpoint | Result |
|---|---|
| `api.moonshot.ai/v1/models` | `HTTP 401 — Invalid Authentication` |
| `api.moonshot.cn/v1/models` | `HTTP 401 — Invalid Authentication` |

Both official Moonshot endpoints reject that key with the identical error, so the app's request format, `Bearer` auth header, base-URL handling, and Keychain storage are all working correctly. The key itself is what's being refused.

**The likely cause:** that key starts with **`sk-kimi-`**. Official Moonshot Open Platform keys are plain **`sk-…`** (no `kimi`). A `sk-kimi-…` key is almost always issued by a **third-party reseller/aggregator**, which runs its *own* API gateway — not `api.moonshot.*`. So to use it, set the **Base URL** to that reseller's endpoint. Otherwise, grab a genuine key from platform.moonshot.cn or platform.moonshot.ai and it'll work against the default URL. (Also note the `.cn` and `.ai` platforms issue *separate* keys — a key for one won't authenticate on the other.)

## The outdated models — my fault, fixed (commit `318e9cb`)

You were right. The hardcoded fallback lists were ancient. Updated to current-generation models:
- **Kimi:** `kimi-latest`, `kimi-k2-0711-preview`, `kimi-k2-turbo-preview`, `moonshot-v1-128k`, `moonshot-v1-auto`, vision preview (no more `moonshot-v1-8k` as the default)
- **Claude:** `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-opus-4-1`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-haiku-4-5` (no more `claude-3-5-*`)
- **OpenAI** `gpt-4.1`/`o3`/`o4-mini`, **GLM** `glm-4.6`/`4.5`, **Doubao 1.5**, **Qwen-max**, **MiniMax-Text-01/M1**

Important: **these are only the offline fallback.** The AI settings screen already auto-calls each provider's live `/models` API when you open it with a working key (and "Refresh Models" does the same), so with a valid key you'll see the provider's *actual current* model list — not this static list. The static list only shows when the live call can't run, which is exactly your situation right now because the key is rejected.

So: fix the key (use the reseller's Base URL, or a real `sk-…` Moonshot key + Refresh Models) and you'll get the up-to-date models automatically. Built clean on macOS; the change is a pure data update.

I tested your key against **every** Moonshot endpoint and auth style:

| Endpoint | Auth | Result |

You'll want to double-check in your Moonshot/Kimi dashboard that the key is **active and copied in full**, and confirm the **exact Base URL** your coding plan documents (some coding plans route through a non-`moonshot.*` host).

You were right that this was a real gap: a "Kimi Code" / coding-plan key speaks the **Anthropic** API (`/v1/messages`), but my app had Kimi hard-locked to the OpenAI format. So even a *valid* coding key couldn't be used. Now you can configure it:

- **API Format:** **Anthropic** ← new picker
- Paste the key → it now sends `/v1/messages` with both `x-api-key` and `Bearer`, parses Anthropic responses, and skips the OpenAI-only `response_format`.

This override works for **any** provider, so it also covers OpenRouter, GLM/Qwen coding gateways, etc.

**Honest caveat:** with the override in place, the request will be correctly Anthropic-shaped — but my test of *this specific key* still got 401 on that Anthropic endpoint, so it won't authenticate until the key issue is resolved. - The grading banner now shows the **actual model it'll use**, so it can't silently mislead again.
- Clear error if a provider genuinely has no vision model.

**You don't need to change any settings** — keep Qwen selected; grading will use `qwen-vl-max` automatically.

Pushed `bfeeb6c`, both platforms green. Three fixes in this round:

## 1. Vocab Save/Save-all now actually save ✅
The buttons were silently dropping any wrong answer whose vocab item wasn't already Chinese-keyed (the store keys on the Chinese field). Now the save:
- falls back to the **correct answer** when the model didn't supply a vocab item,
- **translates English→Chinese** when neither side is Chinese,
- keeps the word as-is as a last resort (never silently dropped),
- and reliably flips the button to **已保存**.

## 2. Grading "data couldn't be read" ✅
That was `qwen-vl-plus` emitting **malformed JSON** (a missing comma — I reproduced it: `Expecting ',' at char 12208`). Now grading **repairs** common JSON mistakes (string-aware, so it won't corrupt text), **retries once**, raises the token budget to 8192, and retries on empty results. Same repair applied to word explanations.

## 3. "Could not generate explanation — request timed out" ✅
The 60s network timeout was too short for big non-streamed responses. Bumped to **180s** (request) / 300s (resource).

## ⭐ One setting change that fixes your experience instantly
You currently have **`qwen-vl-plus`** selected — it's slow for text (→ explanation timeouts) and flaky with JSON (→ grading errors). 

**Set your Qwen model to `qwen-plus`** (Settings → AI → Qwen → Model). Then:
- **Word explanations** use `qwen-plus` → fast & reliable, no timeouts.
- **Workbook grading** automatically uses **`qwen-vl-max`** for vision (the app auto-swaps to a vision model for image tasks) → reliable, valid JSON.

So `qwen-plus` as your main model gives you the best of both. The code fixes above make it robust even if you don't, but `qwen-plus` is the sweet spot.

Both tasks are complete, built on both platforms, committed, and pushed (`8343835`).

## 1. Brand icons ✅
Every AI provider now shows its real vendor logo instead of a generic SF Symbol. I added the SVGs from your `ai-icons` folder as **vector imagesets** in the asset catalog (`brand-<provider>`), so they stay crisp at any size:

| Provider | Icon | Render mode |
|---|---|---|
| Apple Intelligence | `apple.svg` | monochrome (tints to fg, dark-mode safe) |
| OpenAI | `openai.svg` | monochrome |
| Ollama | `ollama.svg` | monochrome |
| Claude | `claude-color.svg` | full color |
| DeepSeek | `deepseek-color.svg` | full color |
| Doubao | `volcengine-color.svg` | full color |
| Qwen | `qwen-color.svg` | full color |
| Kimi | `kimi-color.svg` | full color |
| Zhipu GLM | `chatglm-color.svg` | full color |
| MiniMax | `minimax-color.svg` | full color |

A new shared `ProviderIcon` view renders these everywhere a provider glyph appears (settings pickers, the provider list, the AI-translate buttons, the word-explanation card/badge), and gracefully falls back to the SF Symbol if an asset is ever missing. I verified with `assetutil` that all 10 actually compiled into `Assets.car` with vectors preserved and the right template modes.

Two judgment calls (the only providers without an exact logo in the set) — tell me if you'd prefer a different file:
- **Doubao** → I used the **Volcengine** logo (its API platform). Alternative: `bytedance-color.svg`.
- **Zhipu** → I used **ChatGLM**. Alternative: `zai.svg` (their z.ai brand).

## 2. iOS label wrapping ✅
I added a `.fitSingleLine()` modifier (shrinks the font to fit one line, then ellipsizes — never wraps) and applied it to **17 wrap-prone labels**, the worst offenders being the bilingual provider-name buttons ("Translate with Qwen 通义千问", "Explain with …") and the long Chinese action buttons (e.g. `保存所有错题词汇到词汇本`, `开始批改 · Grade`, `Copy with Pinyin`, `Update Saved Definition`), plus the photo scan-language menu and provider rows.

Note: I committed only my source/asset changes. The repo also had pre-existing uncommitted churn (`project.pbxproj` with duplicate build-file entries — the source of the harmless "Skipping duplicate build file" warnings — plus `Localizable.xcstrings` and logs) that was already modified before this session; I left those untouched since they're unrelated to this task. Let me know if you'd like me to clean up the pbxproj duplicates separately.
